name: Human heart
hook: Four chambers, valves and a pacemaker — the anatomy clues keep circling the same handful of parts.

facts.label: the aorta
facts.statement: The aorta is the largest artery in the body; it leaves the heart's left ventricle and sends blood everywhere, with coronary arteries branching off to feed the heart itself.

facts.label: four chambers
facts.statement: The heart has four chambers: two atria on top and two ventricles below, with the left ventricle pumping blood into the aorta.

facts.label: the pericardium
facts.statement: The pericardium is the two-layered sac around the heart; in the 1890s Daniel Hale Williams made history by repairing it in open-heart surgery.

facts.label: the pacemaker
facts.statement: A pacemaker is an implanted stimulator that regulates the heartbeat; Otis Boykin improved it, and Wilfred Bigelow's hypothermia research helped develop it.

facts.label: heart valves
facts.statement: Heart valves keep blood flowing in one direction; pig valves have been used for decades to replace damaged human ones.

facts.label: cardiology
facts.statement: Cardiology is the branch of medicine that studies the heart; its foundation was laid in 1628 when William Harvey described the circulation of blood.
